clue.text: Very unpleasant, and that's certainly not right!

explanation.surface: An exclamation about something nasty that is plainly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition uses the Latin root: sinister meant left, and something left is literally not right.
explanation.definitionFit: Menacing and evil is the everyday sense; the heraldic sense is on the left-hand side, the opposite of the right.

clue.text: Understand a proverb can divert youngsters

parts.note: to see is to understand
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A wise saying that keeps children amused.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground plank on which children ride up and down, entertaining them.

clue.text: No backward city, it gets a mention

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: backward means the following words are read from the end

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
taken as written

explanation.surface: A town no one praises still gets talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns EC and IT together to give TICE; EC is the postcode for the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief written comment or reference is a notice.

clue.text: Woman modelling a man's hat

indicators.note: modelling something shapes it anew, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A woman wears a man's hat as a model.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name stands for a woman.

clue.text: Small creatures-some may be left standing

indicators.note: some of the words are used, so part of the run left standing gives the letters

explanation.surface: Some little animals may survive a cull.
explanation.definitionFit: Young newts are small amphibians.

clue.text: Scuttles a ship with a cargo of wildfowl

explanation.surface: Someone sinks a vessel loaded with ducks and geese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scuttles' looks like sinking a ship, but here it means hurries off.
explanation.definitionFit: To scuttle is to run with quick short steps, which is what one who scoots does.

clue.text: Shut down before end of August for recess

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: to close is to shut down

indicators.note: the end of the word August is its last letter

explanation.surface: A business closes for the late-summer holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A small room or cupboard set into a wall is an alcove or recess.

clue.text: Pass but striking and not without admirers

parts.note: workers on strike are out
someone who has been dated has had admirers

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned yet striking and much courted.
explanation.walkthrough: The page loses the accent of Passé, meaning old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean no longer fashionable.

clue.text: Shivers as the stars appear

indicators.note: the stars appear in a new form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone trembles as night falls.
explanation.definitionFit: To shiver something is to break it into pieces.

clue.text: Judge times tea break

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it apart, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge takes regular tea breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity is to make a rough calculation of it.

clue.text: Left one with a most important part to play

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who departed is told they had a leading role.
explanation.walkthrough: Portia is the heroine of Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, a celebrated leading role.
explanation.definitionFit: The role is a major stage part, the leading lady in a Shakespeare comedy.

clue.text: People who are late occupy his attention

definitions.text: People who are late occupy his attention

parts.words: People who are late occupy his attention
parts.note: the late here are the dead, whose deaths this official investigates

explanation.definitionFit: An official who holds inquests into deaths deals with the deceased.

clue.text: Like college-head object to rise

parts.note: as means like, in the same way

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of college

parts.note: an end is an object or aim

explanation.surface: A head of a college objects to a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes only the first letter, C, of 'college'.

clue.text: Giving carte blanche to the French rave

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for the
to rant is to rave

explanation.surface: Someone lets the French rant freely.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives others a free hand is permissive and accepting.

clue.text: Lay clutching thin covering

parts.note: a lay is a wager or bet
lank means thin or lean

explanation.surface: A gambler grabbing a thin wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed covering or any layer that covers something.

clue.text: Everybody in entertain, ment seems frivolous

parts.note: a show is a piece of entertainment
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A complaint that all of show business is lightweight.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'entertain, ment' as one word broken by a stray comma: entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking depth of thought or feeling, superficial.

clue.text: Tackle retreating sol, diets for example

clue.text: Carol carries little cash, which is discerning

clue.text: Forwarded about ten cents as a deposit

parts.note: sent means forwarded
a dime is ten cents

explanation.surface: Ten cents mailed as a down payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid is a deposit.

clue.text: Many a worker is not able

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
a worker ant is the typical worker of the insect world

explanation.surface: A workforce that just cannot do the job.
explanation.definitionFit: The contraction says cannot, i.e. lacks the ability.

clue.text: Infuriated grandee in revolt

indicators.note: a thing in revolt is turned over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman enraged by an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean made very cross.

clue.text: Worm serving summons on a fellow

parts.note: a writ is a legal summons

explanation.surface: A process server hands a man a summons.

clue.text: An Irishman in a film

parts.note: Pat is a typical Irish name
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A thin surface layer formed on metal or wood with age.

parts.note: dad is father
O is zero, nothing

clue.text: Being by the water, liked sea to be rough

clue.text: Puff after middle-age-obtain this helpful device

explanation.walkthrough: 'middle-age' reads as a stage of life, but 'middle' is the selection signal working on 'age'; 'Puff' is an advertisement, not breath.
